strategy.thesis: Corporate venture fund of Singtel investing in seed to growth-stage companies with strategic relevance to the Singtel Group across 5G/enterprise, data privacy/security, green-tech and AI; the US$250M AI Growth Fund targets customer engagement, network operations, cyber security, IT automation and enterprise/vertical AI.

summary.en: Singtel Innov8 is the corporate venture capital arm of Singapore telco Singtel, established in 2010. It runs a US$250M evergreen fund plus a US$250M AI Growth Fund (US$500M total), writing US$1–5M checks into seed-to-growth startups strategically relevant to the Singtel Group, with over 120 investments globally and a reported 26% IRR since a 2021 strategic reset.

summary.en: SPH Ventures is the S$100 million corporate venture fund of Singapore Press Holdings, investing in early-growth technology companies globally with a focus on consumer tech and media. Typical tickets are around S$1-2m, up to S$5m per round; portfolio includes ViSenze, TheLorry and Snapcart.

strategy.thesis: Razer's early-stage venture arm, investing in seed and Series A startups globally that add strategic value to the Razer gaming ecosystem across gaming/esports, IoT/consumer hardware, deep tech (AI, AR/VR, blockchain) and sustainability.

summary.en: zVentures is the corporate venture arm of gaming-hardware company Razer, launched in 2016 with an initial commitment of up to US$30 million. It invests US$100K–US$1M into seed and Series A startups globally that add strategic value to the Razer ecosystem (gaming, IoT/consumer hardware, deep tech, sustainability, Web3). Operates out of Singapore and Irvine, California.

strategy.thesis: The corporate venture arm of Singapore internet group Sea Ltd (Shopee, Garena, SeaMoney), launched in 2021 with US$1bn to invest in consumer and enterprise technology developers and build an ecosystem around Sea's offerings. Wound down in 2023.

summary.en: Sea Capital was the corporate venture arm of Singapore internet giant Sea Ltd, launched in March 2021 with US$1 billion to invest in consumer and enterprise technology, led by ex-Hillhouse partner David Ma (whose Composite Capital Management Sea acquired). Sea stopped new equity investing in 2022 and wound the unit down in June 2023, so it is now inactive.

strategy.thesis: The corporate venture capital arm of Telkom Indonesia (the country's largest telco) and the largest CVC in Indonesia. Multi-stage global investor across fintech, healthtech, deep tech, agritech and enterprise, driving synergy value back into the Telkom ecosystem.

summary.en: MDI Ventures is the corporate venture capital arm of Telkom Indonesia, founded in 2015 and headquartered in Jakarta. It is Indonesia's largest CVC with about US$830M total committed AUM across multiple funds (incl. a $500M later-stage fund, $150M Centauri Fund and $40M Arise Fund), 80+ portfolio companies and several unicorns and IPO exits (Geniee, WeBuy Global).

strategy.thesis: Corporate venture capital arm of Telkomsel (Indonesia's largest mobile operator), investing across seed to Series B in startups aligned with Telkomsel's strategic priorities: digital lifestyle, digital enablement/empowerment and emerging technologies.

summary.en: Telkomsel Ventures (formerly Telkomsel Mitra Inovasi / TMI, est. 2019) is the corporate venture arm of Indonesia's largest mobile operator Telkomsel. Its first fund of USD 40 million backed 17 companies; it closed a second flagship fund of over $40 million in 2023, investing seed to Series B across digital lifestyle, enablement and emerging tech. Portfolio includes Halodoc, Kredivo, Evermos and PrivyID.
summary.local: Telkomsel Ventures (sebelumnya Telkomsel Mitra Inovasi / TMI) adalah lengan modal ventura korporat dari operator seluler terbesar Indonesia, Telkomsel. Dana pertamanya senilai USD 40 juta mendanai 17 perusahaan, dan pada 2023 menyiapkan dana flagship kedua untuk mendukung ekosistem startup Indonesia.

strategy.thesis: Grab's innovation/venture arm, supporting growth-stage Southeast Asian technology companies via the Grab Ventures Velocity scale-up program and select strategic investments that leverage Grab's regional super-app ecosystem (mobility, deliveries, payments).

summary.en: Grab Ventures is the innovation/venture arm of Singapore-based super-app Grab. Its flagship Grab Ventures Velocity (GVV) is a scale-up accelerator for post-seed/growth-stage Southeast Asian startups (cohorts of ~5-10, ~16 weeks, no direct cash) that gives portfolio companies pilot access to Grab's ecosystem; Grab may also make select strategic investments in synergistic startups.

strategy.thesis: Early-to-growth-stage, sector-agnostic high-conviction investor established as the venture arm of GoTo/Gojek (now operating independently as Argor Capital, with GoTo remaining an LP). Portfolio spans fintech, aquaculture/agritech and gaming.

summary.en: Argor Capital Management (formerly Go-Ventures / GoTo Ventures, est. 2018) was established as the venture arm of Indonesian super-app GoTo/Gojek and rebranded in 2023 to operate independently, with GoTo remaining a limited partner. It closed Fund I at $175M (2020) and Fund II at $240M, investing early-to-growth-stage across Southeast Asia and India in companies like eFishery, Pluang and Mobile Premier League.

summary.en: Kickstart Ventures, founded in 2012, is the Philippines' largest corporate venture capital firm and a wholly-owned subsidiary of Globe Telecom (Ayala group). It has grown from a US$2.4M corporate incubator to about US$255 million in AUM, including managing Ayala Corporation's US$150M ACTIVE Fund, and has made 70+ investments in early- to mid-growth tech startups across fintech, AI, healthtech and logistics.

strategy.thesis: Vietnam's first tech unicorn (gaming/Zalo/cloud) makes strategic balance-sheet investments to expand its product and industry ecosystem, including e-commerce (Tiki), B2B commerce (Telio) and logistics (EcoTruck).

summary.en: VNG Corporation, Vietnam's first tech unicorn (gaming, Zalo messenger, cloud), acts as a corporate strategic investor, deploying capital from its balance sheet into Vietnamese tech startups to expand its ecosystem. Notable bets include a stake in e-commerce platform Tiki, $22.5m into B2B platform Telio, and investments in EcoTruck and Got It — though it wrote off several (Telio, EcoTruck, Tiki) in 2024.
